scope: Three frozen convenience-selected Codex root-task inputs from one Mac. Bounded Apple overlay versus the offline heuristic, both using scored with keep_score_threshold 0.5. Mechanism qualification only; separate from the 729-session study and 114-root development comparison.
interpretation: The Apple overlay executed successfully and was more conservative on these three inputs, with longer observed wall time. More literal retention came with two no-op cases and much less projected reduction; this establishes no task-quality, cost, latency or backend-superiority claim.
retention_accounting: All variants use 192 baseline probes. For the Apple variant, 128 of 192 retained probes are derived from its two unchanged no-plan inputs; only the remaining 64 probes were checked against its rewritten output.
coverage: The Apple model overlays at most 32 selected candidates per input. Successful overlays covered 92 of 92 selected candidates; candidates outside that bound retain heuristic scores. That expected heuristic remainder is distinct from failed-backend fallback.
limitations: Three convenience inputs from one Mac; this qualifies the Apple-plus-cutoff execution mechanism only.
Both variants use the preregistered 0.5 threshold; this does not tune or establish an optimal threshold.
Apple overlays at most 32 selected candidates; unscored candidates retain heuristic scores. Heuristic remainder is expected coverage, distinct from backend failure fallback.
Literal string survival is not semantic understanding, task correctness, or resume qualification. Protected-tail probes can be absent.
Token changes are offline estimates, not measured provider-billed savings, live context, cache cost, or productivity.
One pass without repeatability or model cold/warm control; timings are descriptive and model outputs may vary.
Raw inputs, input hashes, selected line positions, prompts, responses and missed probes are never public.
privacy: Aggregate methodology only. Private inputs, input hashes, selected line positions, prompts, responses, missed probes and per-input records are excluded.
